title: A compound meaning is transparent unless a whole-form override is licensed
summary: A bounded compositionality hypothesis says a multi-part written unit inherits the meanings of its visible parts unless a separately licensed whole-form override is present.

design.mechanism: default compositional transparency with explicit idiom override
design.unit: complete multi-part units paired with their component occurrences and any whole-form override
design.prediction: Changing one component should change the interpreted unit in the corresponding component dimension; only a licensed override may block that change.
design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial packaging could produce the same surface distribution without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: A component changes while the unit remains semantically identical in matched contexts with no override, or a licensed override fails to block component substitution.
design.principal_risk: Component meanings and override licenses are unavailable. Near historical composition and whole-form cards; unresolved whether this is a distinct semantic claim or a restatement of compositional rendering.
